narration: Seventy-three percent of people get a tax refund every year and feel like they won. But a refund means you overpaid — and the IRS gave you zero percent interest on that loan.
visual: Envelope opening to reveal a refund check for $2,753. A glowing badge appears: '0% INTEREST'. Red X through 'WINNING'.

narration: Here's how it works. Your W-4 form tells your employer how much to withhold from every paycheck. Most people fill it out once when they're hired — and never touch it again.
visual: A W-4 document icon. Person silhouette sitting at desk signing it. Calendar pages fast-forward through years. W-4 collects dust.

narration: The average refund is $2,753 — that's $229 sitting with the government every single month. Meanwhile, if you're carrying credit card debt at 22%, you're literally paying to give them a free loan.
visual: Two side-by-side bars: 'YOUR REFUND: $2,753' and 'CREDIT CARD RATE: 22%'. Credit card SVG with flames growing upward.

narration: Here's the real cost. That $2,753 invested every January instead of waiting for April — at eight percent returns — grows to four hundred and seventeen thousand dollars over forty years.
visual: Coin stack growing into a mountain. Counter animating from $2,753 up to $417,000. Arrow curving steeply upward.

narration: You can fix this in five minutes. Go to the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator, update your W-4, and submit it to HR. Your very next paycheck gets bigger — permanently.
visual: Phone screen showing IRS logo. W-4 form with a checkmark. Paycheck graphic showing amount increasing with upward arrow.

narration: Most people spend their whole career handing the government free loans and calling refunds a gift. The fix is completely free, takes five minutes, and starts this pay period. Go do it.
visual: Person silhouette holding a growing stack of coins. Bold text: 'UPDATE YOUR W-4 TODAY'. Red arrow pointing up. Piggy bank filling up.
